The Farmstead

Turning 105 Years of Family Stewardship Into the Next 20+ Years of Kingdom Impact.

I want to tell you about something Kelly and I are trying to do with our Farmstead. Our family has been farming this land for 105 years. It's approximately 1,000 acres, and there's something about knowing that generations before us worked this ground, cared for it, built on it, and passed it forward that makes us feel a responsibility for what happens next.

In the middle of the farm sits two acres of memories called The Farmstead. Over the years, we've developed a beautiful gathering place there. It has become a successful wedding and event venue with three buildings, approximately 7,700 square feet of facilities, and an operating business that has consistently generated revenue.

The season

We don't want to sell this to someone who sees it as just another piece of real estate.

Kelly and I have reached an interesting season. We don't want to sell this piece of the farm to someone who simply sees it as another piece of real estate. We also don't want to spend the next 20 years personally operating a wedding venue. And yet we don't want the story to end.

We want to change the purpose of the Farmstead without losing the place.

Our vision is to transform the Farmstead from primarily a wedding venue into a self-sustaining Christian hospitality and retreat center that can serve people for the next 20 years and hopefully far beyond us.

Something in between.

Not a traditional nonprofit. Not a traditional for-profit.

Not a traditional nonprofit retreat center dependent upon donations every year. And not a traditional for-profit venue whose primary purpose is maximizing profit. Something in between.

A business with a Kingdom purpose

The Farmstead would remain a professionally operated for-profit business.

It would continue hosting weddings, corporate retreats, celebrations and private events. Those activities would provide the economic engine that allows the property to support itself. But its deeper purpose would change. We envision the Farmstead increasingly becoming a place for:

Marriage retreats

Pastor and ministry-leader renewal

Christian leadership retreats

Church gatherings

Spiritual formation experiences

Executive retreats

Next-generation experiences

Families who need a place to reconnect

People who simply need space to hear God again

Hospitality becomes ministry. Mission determines why the property exists.

Why we're looking for 10–15 families

A small group of Kingdom-minded families, rather than one conventional buyer.

Rather than finding one conventional buyer for the Farmstead, we're exploring whether a small group of Kingdom-minded families might use charitable capital they've already set aside to help make this possible.

We're working with Impact Foundation to explore structuring the Farmstead as an impact investment. The concept is approximately 10–15 families participating at roughly $100,000–$150,000 each, creating approximately $1.75 million of impact capital.

That capital would enable the new enterprise to acquire the Farmstead property, facilities, equipment and operating business and establish the next chapter of the Farmstead on a sustainable financial footing.

The double impact

A double-impact opportunity for your charitable capital.

Through an Impact Foundation Impact Account, charitable capital can be invested in an approved mission-driven for-profit enterprise.

First

The Farmstead puts it to work

The Farmstead puts that capital to work immediately by preserving and operating a place dedicated to Christian hospitality and transformation.

Then

Capital returns, and gives again

As the enterprise generates investment distributions and ultimately returns capital, those proceeds go back into the Impact Account, not into your pocket, to be invested again for impact or granted to another charity. It is double impact.

So the same charitable dollar has the potential to create impact more than once. It can help create the Farmstead today. And as capital is returned in the future, it can help fund another Kingdom initiative tomorrow.

The same charitable dollar has the potential to create impact more than once.

Not a charity constantly asking for money. A sustainable Kingdom asset.

What success would look like

Imagine this place 10 years from now.

Hundreds of couples have come through marriage experiences here. Pastors who were exhausted have found rest here. Leadership teams have gotten away from the noise and rediscovered their purpose. Churches have gathered here. Young leaders have encountered God here. Families have celebrated weddings and milestones here.

And the revenue from weddings, corporate gatherings and other commercial events has helped pay for the infrastructure that makes all of that possible.

The next steps

Could something stewarded for 105 years become something the Kingdom stewards for the next generation?

Kelly and I could simply sell the Farmstead. There is real estate here. There is an operating business. There are buildings and assets. We have conventional options. But before we do that, we're asking a different question: could something our family has stewarded for 105 years become something the Kingdom stewards for the next generation? That's the opportunity we're exploring.

We have already taken the steps to value the property and the business along with the assets. Impact Foundation has determined the investment meets its requirements. We have secured the proper legal and tax counsel involved, and we believe the economics and impact expectations are transparent and reasonable.

We're not looking for people to rescue something. We're looking for a small group of people to partner with us to impact thousands of people through the Farmstead.

The invitation

Would you consider deploying $100,000–$150,000 of charitable capital into a sustainable Christian gathering place for the next 20 years and beyond?

You'd be helping preserve something that already exists—no renovations are needed. You'd be helping change what it exists for. And together, we'd have the opportunity to turn 105 years of family stewardship into decades of Kingdom impact. That's the vision.
